definitions.gloss: to appear; to show oneself; to come into view
definitions.explanation: Describes someone or something becoming visible, often after being absent, hidden, or anticipated. Used for both physical appearances and figurative emergence.

examples.japanese: {雲|くも}の{間|あいだ}から{月|つき}が{姿|すがた}を{現|あらわ}した。
examples.english: The moon appeared from between the clouds.

examples.japanese: {犯人|はんにん}はまだ{姿|すがた}を{現|あらわ}していない。
examples.english: The culprit has not yet shown himself.

examples.japanese: {駅前|えきまえ}に{新|あたら}しい{高層|こうそう}ビルが{姿|すがた}を{現|あらわ}し、{街|まち}の{景色|けしき}がすっかり{変|か}わった。
examples.english: A new high-rise building appeared in front of the station, and the scenery of the town completely changed.

notes:
USAGE:
A set phrase combining {姿|すがた} (figure, form) with {現|あらわ}す (to reveal). Often used in narrative and news contexts to describe someone or something coming into view. The subject can be a person, animal, building, or natural phenomenon.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {姿|すがた}を{消|け}す: to disappear — the opposite expression, meaning to vanish from sight
- {現|あらわ}れる: to appear — a simpler, single-verb alternative without the nuance of revealing a full figure
